title: Pandya Cleared by BCCI Centre of Excellence. He Has Not Played an ODI in Fifteen Months.
excerpt: The all-rounder passed his fitness tests after a back injury during IPL 2026. Rohit Sharma's clearance is still pending. India's ODI series against Afghanistan begins Saturday in Dharamsala.
body:
His back gave way during the IPL. Mumbai Indians finished ninth. Reports surfaced that he wanted out. For most of the last fortnight, Hardik Pandya's name in India's ODI squad for the Afghanistan series looked more like a placeholder than a guarantee.

On Friday, the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bangalore changed that. Pandya passed every fitness test the medical staff put him through — bowling spells, batting drills, the high-intensity running benchmarks — and was cleared to join the squad. It had been fifteen months since his last ODI, a Champions Trophy match against New Zealand in Dubai in March 2024.

## The Injury and the IPL Fallout

Pandya sustained a back injury during the IPL 2026 season, a recurring problem that has shadowed his career since the stress fracture that sidelined him for the better part of 2019. He missed four of Mumbai Indians' fourteen matches and, when he did play, looked a diminished version of himself — 206 runs and four wickets across ten games, captaining a side that never seriously threatened the playoff places.

The IPL exit was followed by a quieter storm. Reports from Dainik Jagran's Abhishek Tripathi, who first broke the fitness clearance on X, indicated that Pandya had communicated his desire to part ways with Mumbai Indians. The franchise that built him, and that he captained to a title in 2017, may have seen its last season with the Baroda all-rounder.

None of that matters now, at least not for the next three weeks. What matters is that Pandya checked into the CoE on June 2, spent four days undergoing assessment, and walked out with a clean bill of health.

## Rohit Sharma's Fitness Remains Uncertain

Pandya's clearance is one half of a fitness equation that still has an unknown variable. Rohit Sharma, who injured his hamstring during the IPL and played his last few matches mostly as an impact player, has not yet received clearance from the CoE. India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak, speaking after the one-off Test win over Afghanistan in Mullanpur, was careful with his words.

"I have honestly not got the news whether they have been cleared or not," Kotak told Revsportz. "But I'm sure they will be there. Whatever I heard, they are fine — but they have to go and do that fitness test."

With Virat Kohli already ruled out after tearing his hamstring in the IPL final — Yashasvi Jaiswal has replaced him — India's ODI batting order is missing two of its three senior pillars. If Rohit does not get cleared, Shubman Gill, who captained the Test side to an innings-and-300-run win last week, will lead a squad that is increasingly young, increasingly unfamiliar with the 50-over format, and increasingly focused on one thing: the 2027 World Cup in South Africa.

## Why This Series Matters for NRIs

The three-match ODI series — June 14 in Dharamsala, June 17 in Lucknow, June 20 in Chennai — is India's first significant ODI assignment since the Champions Trophy triumph in early 2024. For the diaspora, it arrives during a week when the FIFA World Cup will dominate every other sports conversation in the United States, Canada, and the UK. Cricket fans in those countries will have to carve out their own viewing windows, but the matches are worth the effort.

This is not a dead rubber against a weak opponent. Afghanistan's ODI squad includes Rashid Khan, Ibrahim Zadran, Azmatullah Omarzai, and Rahmanullah Gurbaz — four players who can single-handedly change a match. And India are using this series to audition combinations that might fly to South Africa in 2027. Gurnoor Brar and Harsh Dubey, both uncapped, will get their first taste of international cricket. Prince Yadav, the left-arm wrist-spinner, could get a game.

For Pandya specifically, the questions are not small. Can his body handle ten overs in 40-degree heat? Can he bat at number six and finish an innings the way he did in the Champions Trophy? Can he be the player India need him to be for another eighteen months?

The CoE has said yes to the first question. The rest, Pandya will have to answer on the field.

For NRIs, the significance of this series extends beyond mere entertainment. The performance of players like Pandya can influence the perception of Indian cricket abroad, impacting fan engagement and the diaspora's connection to their roots. Additionally, successful performances can boost remittances as cricket continues to be a unifying force for Indians living abroad, fostering a sense of pride and community. As they tune in to watch the matches, many NRIs will feel a renewed connection to their homeland, reinforcing family ties and cultural identity.

## The Squad

India's ODI squad: Shubman Gill (c), Rohit Sharma (subject to fitness), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shreyas Iyer (vc), KL Rahul (wk), Ishan Kishan (wk), Hardik Pandya, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna, Prince Yadav, Gurnoor Brar, Harsh Dubey.

*The first ODI is on Saturday, June 14 at the HPCA Stadium in Dharamsala. All matches start at 1:30 PM IST (4:00 AM EDT / 1:00 AM PDT).*
